_what: The tools the records tool server lists over MCP (src/serve/mcp.rs): one for each operation of the records door (tools/records-door/README.md), named as the door names it. The server refuses to start when an operation of src/records/mod.rs OPERATIONS is not listed here or a listed name is not an operation. Every tool takes the call's request key as `call_key` and, for a read, `after_byte` (settings.json `call_fields`), which the engine adds; a tool's other fields are the door's input.

tools.name: records:read
tools.description: One record: {id, type, value}, value null when the record is absent or of another type.

id.description: The record's id (text without a slash)

after_byte.description: Where the next byte page of an answer too big for one message starts (the previous page's next_after_byte)

call_key.description: The call's request key, which the engine adds to the call; a write answers its first receipt when it is sent again under the same key

tools.name: records:list
tools.description: One page of the records of a type, greatest id first unless reverse is false: {records: [{id, type, value}], next}. prefix, above and below bound the ids; after is a previous page's next; fields narrows each value to those top-level fields ([] gives ids and types only); where keeps the rows whose fields equal the values given and limit then bounds the rows shown. A declared order and a typed view are not answered.

order.description: Not answered: a call that names a declared order is refused

after_byte.description: Where the next byte page of an answer too big for one message starts (the previous page's next_after_byte)

call_key.description: The call's request key, which the engine adds to the call; a write answers its first receipt when it is sent again under the same key

tools.name: records:search
tools.description: The records whose text holds every asked word, ranked: {question, terms, results: [{id, type, title, said, score, address, found_in, places}], unavailable, pending}. With type only that type is searched; with none, every type.

after_byte.description: Where the next byte page of an answer too big for one message starts (the previous page's next_after_byte)

call_key.description: The call's request key, which the engine adds to the call; a write answers its first receipt when it is sent again under the same key

tools.name: records:write
tools.description: Write whole records in one transaction: each {id, type, value | null, expected?}; null removes; expected is null (the record must be absent) or {type, value} (it must be exactly that). Answers {changed, write_count}; the same request key sent again answers the first receipt and changes nothing.

call_key.description: The call's request key, which the engine adds to the call; a write answers its first receipt when it is sent again under the same key

tools.name: records:result
tools.description: The receipt of an earlier records:write or workspace:write, given its original request key, operation and input; it never writes. A write that left no receipt is not said to have had no effect.

after_byte.description: Where the next byte page of an answer too big for one message starts (the previous page's next_after_byte)

call_key.description: This read's own request key, which the engine adds

tools.name: workspace:read
tools.description: The payloads of exact workspace labels: {status, content_type, text}, text the JSON {records: {label: payload}} with a label that is not there absent. Prefixes must be an empty array.

after_byte.description: Where the next byte page of an answer too big for one message starts (the previous page's next_after_byte)

call_key.description: The call's request key, which the engine adds to the call; a write answers its first receipt when it is sent again under the same key

tools.name: workspace:write
tools.description: Write the payloads of workspace labels in one transaction: {writes: [{address_label, payload}]}. Answers {changed, write_count}; the same request key answers the first receipt.

call_key.description: The call's request key, which the engine adds to the call; a write answers its first receipt when it is sent again under the same key
